heroCopy: Find your best chance to see the Northern Lights in Iceland tonight — with aurora activity, clouds, darkness and moonlight combined into one simple score.
watchExplanation: Green shows aurora activity, grey shows cloud cover — the band runs from sunset to sunrise.
placesIntro: Aurora activity is broadly the same across Iceland — clouds determine where it can be seen. The score combines activity, clouds, darkness and moonlight; 100 is a perfect night.
mapLegend: Point size and colour show tonight's score; the grey ring shows cloud cover.
mapClick: Click a place to see its watch.
dataIntro: Three open data services, regularly refreshed by the backend. No registration, no passwords.
dataAuroraText: NOAA SWPC measures disturbances in Earth's magnetic field and publishes the Kp index together with a forecast for the coming hours.
dataWeatherText: MET Norway provides an hourly forecast for each location. Wind chill is calculated from temperature and wind speed using the standard formula.
dataDarknessText: sunrisesunset.io calculates sunset, darkness and moon position from each location's coordinates.
footerText: Northseek shows probabilities, not promises. The aurora does its own thing.
auroraLowText: A faint arc low in the north. Darkness, clear skies and distance from city lights are important.
auroraNormalText: Visible well outside built-up areas. This is the most common situation on a good aurora night.
auroraElevatedText: The light reaches higher into the sky and can be seen across much of Iceland, including the outskirts of towns.
auroraStormText: The aurora often spreads across the whole country and may be visible from built-up areas. Movement and colours become more noticeable.
auroraStrongText: Bright, active light overhead, potentially even in central Reykjavík.
auroraSevereText: Rare. The aurora can fill the sky and may be visible far south of Iceland.
bzQuietText: The solar wind magnetic field is mostly pointing north — little energy for aurora activity right now.
bzPickingText: Bz is pointing south, which is favourable — aurora activity becomes more likely if other conditions are right.
bzActiveText: Bz is strongly negative — good chances of active aurora during the next few hours.
bzStrongText: Bz is very negative — an unusually favourable situation. The aurora may become bright and visible across much of Iceland.
scoreSentenceLow: Activity only reaches Kp {kp} tonight. Clear skies and patience are needed to see much.
scoreSentenceCloudy: Activity is good, but clouds cover {place} for much of the night. {best} is clearer — that is where the outlook is best.
scoreSentencePartial: Partly cloudy, but skies should clear after midnight. Activity peaks around Kp {kp} at about the same time.
scoreSentenceClear: Mostly clear skies and activity peaks around Kp {kp}. This is a night to go outside.
feelsFreezing: It is {temp}° outside but feels like {feels}° — freezing on the skin.
feelsWind: It is {temp}° outside and feels like {feels}° in the wind.
feelsCalm: It is {temp}° outside with almost no wind.
moonRise: The moon is {percent}% full and rises at {time}.
bestWindow: The best window is {from}–{to}, with {cloud}% cloud cover.
noWindow: No useful viewing window tonight. Check the list below — elsewhere in Iceland it may be clearer.
currentKp: Kp {kp} now, peaking around {time}. This is a forecast for tonight, not a real-time measurement — see “Right now” below.
scaleNote: The marker is at Kp 2 — aurora is generally visible here from around this level because Iceland lies beneath the auroral oval.
noSpaceWeather: Real-time solar-wind data is not available at the moment.
spaceWindDelay: Changes in the solar wind can take 30–60 minutes to show up in the sky here.
measuredBy: Measured by the DSCOVR satellite between Earth and the Sun, republished by NOAA SWPC. For local magnetic disturbances, see real-time measurements from Leirvogur (University of Iceland Institute of Earth Sciences).
nearestLocation: The nearest location is {place}, {distance} km away.
browserNoLocation: Your browser does not support location. Choose a place from the list.
dataNotReady: The data is not ready yet — try again in a moment.
locationFailed: We couldn't get your location. Choose a place from the list.
backendError: Could not load data from the backend ({error}). Make sure the server is running.
clickToWatch: Click to see this location's watch.
kpNow: Kp {kp} now, highest around {time}. This is a forecast for tonight, not a real-time measurement — see “Right now” below.
solarWindFast: The solar-wind speed is also unusually high, which broadens the auroral oval and can bring the lights farther south.
densityHigh: The particle density is also high, which can produce stronger and brighter colours.
